video_title: Tim Thomas NBA Draft Trade Secret & Snubbing LeBron James: Vets

quotes.speaker: Tim Thomas
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Thomas on being traded by the Nets shortly after being drafted
quotes.excerpt: I got drafted by the Nets. I thought I was going to be a Net. But Keith Van Horn had the power agent in David Falk, and I got traded 10 minutes later.
quotes.quote: I got drafted by the Nets. I thought I was going to be a Net. But Keith Van Horn had the power agent in David Falk, and I got traded 10 minutes later because Keith said, 'I can't go play in Philly. Derrick Coleman is the power forward, I ain't starting over him. I can't run the floor with AI and Jerry Stackhouse. Trade me right now.' And that's how the trade happened.

quotes.speaker: Tim Thomas
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Thomas on the talent level of the 1996 high school class
quotes.excerpt: Special, special class. Myself, Mike Bibby, Jermaine O'Neal, Rip Hamilton, Kobe Bryant, Lester Earl, Shaheen Holloway. So many talented guys.
quotes.quote: Special, special class. Myself, Mike Bibby, Jermaine O'Neal, Rip Hamilton, Kobe Bryant, Lester Earl, Shaheen Holloway, Steve Jackson, Corey Benjamin, Mateen Cleaves. So many talented guys.

quotes.speaker: Tim Thomas
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Thomas on being ranked ahead of Kobe Bryant in high school
quotes.excerpt: I was ranked ahead of Kobe. Kobe actually came to play with me, Vince Carter, Rip Hamilton, Kevin Freeman. We were all on the same AAU team.
quotes.quote: I was ranked ahead of Kobe. Kobe actually came to play with me, Vince Carter, Rip Hamilton, Kevin Freeman. We were all on the same AAU team. So Kobe got to kind of get a feel for the lay of the land. That team is considered the best AAU team ever assembled.

quotes.speaker: Tim Thomas
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Thomas on why he chose to play college basketball
quotes.excerpt: What helped me a whole lot was the decision that I made to go to college. It slowed everything down for me.
quotes.quote: What helped me a whole lot was the decision that I made to go to college. It slowed everything down for me. You are going through grammar school and high school with this decision. Then your senior year comes, you have this money on the table, you have the NBA on the table. Going to college gave me an opportunity to see who was really around for what.

quotes.speaker: Tim Thomas
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Thomas on why he chose to play for Villanova
quotes.excerpt: Going to Nova was an easy decision because they had guys already there that was already on the board.
quotes.quote: Going to Nova was an easy decision because they had guys already there that was already on the board. They had Chuck Kornegay, he was on the board power forward. You had Alvin Williams, obviously, you had Jason Lawson, and we had some talented guys that was coming behind them too, and John Celestand and Malik Allen. It was a talented bunch, man, and I felt like if I went there, it would show me the ropes a little bit.

quotes.speaker: Tim Thomas
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Thomas on his near-signing with the Spurs
quotes.excerpt: Initially, I was going to sign with the Spurs. Pop reached out maybe two weeks ahead of time.
quotes.quote: Initially, I was going to sign with the Spurs. Pop reached out maybe two weeks ahead of time, once he knew I was trying to get out of the deal with Chicago. And I just looked at their roster and I was like, 'Man, there's no way I'm going to be able to play.' Because I wanted one more deal. And I was like, 'There's no way Pop's going to be able to play and showcase myself in a half a season going right into the playoffs.'

quotes.speaker: Tim Thomas
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Thomas on joining the Suns
quotes.excerpt: When Phoenix called, they were like, 'Man, it's not a matter of if we want you, we got to have you.'
quotes.quote: When Phoenix called, they were like, 'Man, it's not a matter of if we want you, we got to have you.' And I was like, 'What you mean?' And they were like, 'Man, we got Amare Stoudemire out and Kurt Thomas out hurt. They done for the year. You coming in, you playing 30, 35, no matter what. Work your way into shape, you coming in, you playing.' And that was a tell-tale sign for me.

quotes.speaker: Tim Thomas
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Thomas on Jalen Brunson as a Knicks player
quotes.excerpt: Is Jalen Brunson the best Knick ever? That's debatable. I don't want to get into that.
quotes.quote: Is Jalen Brunson the best Knick ever? That's debatable. I don't want to get into that because there's so many greats. But what I will say this, I will say this, being a Villanova guy, those three guys are just winners, man. They know how to win. They will figure it out and they will find a way to win.

quotes.speaker: Tim Thomas
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Thomas on the Knicks' championship prospects
quotes.excerpt: The New York Knicks is playing in it this year, not the Celtics. We're in it this year.
quotes.quote: The New York Knicks is playing in it this year, not the Celtics. We're in it this year.

quotes.speaker: Tim Thomas
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Thomas on playing for Lenny Wilkens
quotes.excerpt: I used to love playing for Lenny Wilkens. Lenny Wilkens was a player's coach.
quotes.quote: I used to love playing for Lenny Wilkens. Lenny Wilkens was a player's coach. He played and had a great career playing and as a coach. And he just understood us. He really understood us.

quotes.speaker: Tim Thomas
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Thomas on playing for Isaiah Thomas
quotes.excerpt: Playing for Isaiah Thomas was pretty dope. Playing for a Hall of Famer.
quotes.quote: Playing for Isaiah Thomas was pretty dope. Playing for a Hall of Famer. And then later, later in my career, seeing Rick Carlisle do his thing a little bit, playing for Mike D'Antoni, who was a percentage guy. We called him the casino coach because he always played by the numbers.

quotes.speaker: Tim Thomas
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Thomas on the importance of post-game in the modern NBA
quotes.excerpt: I think the NBA is in trouble once that guy gets some low post game.
quotes.quote: I think the NBA is in trouble once that guy gets some low post game. Because if he had anything in the post, it's over. And who's blocking a turnaround jump shot? If he fade a little bit, it's over. Like, who's blocking that?
